newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA STILL INVESTIGATING SVYAZINVEST SALE.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA STILL INVESTIGATING SVYAZINVEST SALE.

text.p: Russia's Federal Service for Currency and Export Control (FSCEC) said on Tuesday it was still investigating the controversial sale of a stake in telecommunications holding company Svyazinvest.

Earlier RIA Novosti news agency said the FSCEC had already prepared its report on the sale which it said contained criticism of "crude violations" of Russia's law on currency regulations and controls.
"At the present time the FSCEC, along with the anti-monopoly commission and the Justice Ministry, is conducting such an (inquiry). But it is not yet completed," the service said in a statement.
"Neither official nor preliminary data on the results of this investigation have been prepared and sent to the government," the statement said.
The sale of a 25 percent plus one share stake in Svyazinvest triggered a furious political row involving several of Russia's most powerful media tycoons and the government's main reformers.

The winning consortium, Cyprus-based Mustcom, bought the stake for $1.875 billion. Ministers hailed the sale, arguably Russia's biggest so far, as fair and transparent and said the proceeds would help pay the salary arrears of the country's impoverished army officers, doctors and teachers.
But critics of the tender said it was a murky transaction between state officials and Mustcom, which is dominated by Uneximbank, Russia's third largest bank.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin ordered an inquiry into the sale on August 1.
